ABSTRACT  
Reliability and cost-effectiveness in the operation of the multiple microgrid (MMG) system depend on the skillful 
management of its energy resources. Traditional energy management approaches are physics-model-based, 
which rely on the precise system parameters (e.g., line parameters) of the electricity and heat network. It is 
difficult to establish the precise system parameters in practice because they depend on a variety of factors. In this 
context, this paper proposes a physics-model-free control framework for the energy management of MMGs with 
heat-electricity energy, consisting of proposed surrogate model and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning 
(MADRL) approach. An important step is to use historical data to train a surrogate model in supervised manner 
that can imitate the realistic power and thermal flow calculations. Meanwhile, the energy management problem 
is reformulated as a Markov game. It is solved by the proposed MADRL-based approach by modeling each MG 
controller as an agent with a specific objective. The historical trajectories representation, parameter space 
technology, and deep dense architecture in reinforcement learning are introduced in MADRL to overcome the 
negative impact brought by the time series data from the input state on the decision-making process and 
construct an efficient exploration mechanism to overcome inefficient optimization of the MMG system in a multi- 
agent setting. During training period of MADRL, the trained surrogate models integrate into the environment of 
the MADRL, which can develop optimal energy management strategy based on the continuous interaction with 
the surrogate models. The proposed surrogate model enabled MADRL approach can reduce the reliance on 
precise physical systems and prevent having an impact on the real system while being trained involving trial and 
error process. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control framework.   
1. Introduction 
A vigorous effort has been made globally to develop renewable en -
ergy sources such as wind and solar power to reduce dependence on 
fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions [1,2] . In this context, micro -
grids (MG) provide an effective way of utilizing distributed renewable 
energy by deploying distributed generators, distributed energy storage, 
and local demands in a decentralized manner [3,4] . The present day 
multi-energy MGs are capable of improving holistic energy utilization 
efficiency through the integration of heterogeneous energy carriers such 
as electrical and thermal energy, despite their typically small size. Due 
to the capacity limitations of an individual MG, there are places where

multiple nearby MGs can exchange energy to reduce total costs and 
bolster the reliability of the power supply [5]. Therefore, the multiple 
MGs (MMGs) with combined heat and power (CHP) can be regard as a 
novel concept with both high energy utilization efficiency and high 
energy allocation potential. To exploit the advantages of MMG with 
CHP, it is necessary to develop energy management for it. Developments 
in energy management for the MMG with CHP system typically classi -
fied into two types: centralized and distributed or decentralized 
approach. 
Ref. [6] uses particle swarm optimization to centrally schedule 
MMGs with the lowest operational costs. However, owing to the high 
levels of real-time necessary for MMG control and the complexity of 
energy management of MMGs, the [6] cannot accomplish the intended 
results. In view of this, [7] presents an imperialist competitive-based 
approach for addressing the energy management issue of MMG with 
CHP system, which has quicker convergence speed and stronger global 
convergence than [6] to try to satisfy high real-time control re -
quirements and achieve better control performance. Centralized control 
is required to process massive volumes of information at a single loca -
tion simultaneously. Because of this characteristic, centralized control 
cannot provide the plug-and-play functionality that is essential for the 
MMG system; centralized control is better suited for stand-alone power 
systems that maintain critical supply and demand balances in an infra -
structure that changes slowly [8]. Additionally, centralized control 
needs to collect the information of all the MGs. Distinct MGs may be 
owned by different parties, and the scheduling of distributed genera -
tions inside each MG may be governed by their own policies and eco -
nomic rules [9]. This may restrict the exchange of information between 
MGs, for concerns of privacy and security. 
In distribution-based and decentralization-based approaches, the 
whole optimization problem is divided into a number of smaller sub -
problems that can be solved in a distributed manner, potentially over -
coming the drawbacks of the centralized approach to some extent. For 
this reason, distributed and decentralized control manner is a trend for 
the energy management of MMGs [10]. To quantify the benefits of 
proactive resource trading among MMGs, [11] proposes a distributed 
alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to optimize syn -
ergistic MMG with CHP activities, which can discover the optimal so -
lution in less iterations. Further, [12] implements the primal dual 
multiplier method to the energy management of MMG in distributed 
manner, which delivers better results in terms of optimized time spent 
and solution accuracy than [11], obtaining the required results. Therein, 
information is shared among MGs to enhance the coordination. How -
ever, such a procedure would increase communication costs, and for 
information sharing reasons, the privacy cannot be protected well. To 
fill the gaps, decentralized control manner is the desired way. The 
decentralized strategy does not necessitate the establishment of 
communication links between controllers. Some of the distributed 
approach’s characteristics, as well as the fact that the control is con -
ducted using just local information, are kept in decentralized control 
manner. In [13], a robust decentralized optimization is presented to 
manage the source in MMG integrated with CHP. To improve the energy 
management of MMG containing CHP, a decentralized bi-level sto -
chastic optimization technique is presented in [14]. Distributed energy 
resources are subject to rapid fluctuations. For instance, due to cloud 
dynamics, the photovoltaic (PV) cell output may fluctuate quickly in a 
matter of seconds. To cope with the fast-changing outputs of PVs, more 
frequent operations of controlled devices are necessary under this 
circumstance. Though the above studies achieve some good results, they 
may hard to respond to the last optimization requirement when DERs 
change dramatically in a short period of time. 
Recently, the emergence of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is 
expected to provide a way to fill the gaps. In the case of other domains, 
the use of DRL has proven to be a viable way to coordinate the operation 
of different system resources in the most efficient manner possible while 
taking into account their specific characteristics and uncertainties. 
Unlike optimization-based approaches, the obtained policy from DRL 
can be used to make end-to-end complex decisions by generating the 
desired action instantly (e.g., within several milliseconds) based on the 
state of the system right after the learning process [15]. A DRL system 
with this characteristic is well suited for applications that involve the 
decision-making process in real-time. Through the integration of DRL’s 
expertise into power system decision-making and control, a flexible tool 
can be developed to overcome the limitations of traditional model-based 
control approaches and to allow fast and effective decision making in 
highly complex situations. In addition, the use of model-free DRL does 
not have to be detrimental to the modeling efforts that are already being 
undertaken; rather, it may regard as a complementary role in order to 
achieve better degrees of adaptability and flexibility. In this way, it has 
the potential to be used as a strategic tool that helps people make de -
cisions that are adaptive, effective, flexible, quick, and forward-looking. 
In today’s constantly changing world, this is a great way to meet the 
needs of a rapidly changing energy landscape [16]. Despite the contin -
uous advancement of DRL application research in energy management, 
current approaches primarily focus on single-agent DRL-based control 
strategies, which limit the application of single-agent DRL to specific 
small-scale scenarios when the operation state dimensions of emerging 
power and energy networks are becoming more and more multidimen -
sional. Problems requiring complex coordination among agents can be 
poorly solved using single-agent DRL approaches [17]. In this regard, 
multi-agent DRL (MADRL) has emerged as a promising active research 
area that merges both the advantages of multi-agent systems and data- 
driven approaches, and it has the ability to efficiently handle decision- 
making problems in an environment with multiple agents, and as such 
is receiving a lot of attention. 
A multi-agent Q-learning based residential multiple energy MG 
(MEMG) energy management approach is proposed in the [18]. 
Although the simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness, it cannot 
solve the continuous state and action space. The fuzzy Q-learning based 
approach, which can overcome the “curse of dimensionality” problem 
that traditional Q-learning may encounter, is proposed in [19] to 
construct a cooperative multi-agent system for managing the energy of 
the MG. The experimental findings demonstrate the ability of the multi- 
agent system to ensure electricity supply and improve the constancy of 
the MG. Nevertheless, fuzzy-Q learning may have sluggish convergence 
and require manual extraction of fuzzy features, making it susceptible to 
local optimum. To lower the computational cost of RL, a sizable research 
effort is still required. To this end, [20] proposes a function approxi -
mation for Q-learning to leverage a diffusion strategy to coordinate the 
actions among multiple agents to manage the energy in the microgrid. 
Simulation results demonstrate its advantages compared to fuzzy-Q 
learning. However, it only utilizes linear mapping to approximate the 
Q-value table, which makes the approximate results insufficient to fully 
characterize the implicit information in the Q-value table. In order to 
better approximate the Q-value table, [21] proposes a multi-agent 
double deep Q network (MADDQN)-based approach for the MG en -
ergy management. Although the simulation results demonstrate its 
effectiveness, each agent need to collect other agents’ information to 
make decision. Taking this approach may carry both the risk of privacy 
leakage and the inevitable cost of communication as well. To avoid these 
drawbacks to a certain extent, [22] proposes a MADDQN-based 
approach that uses the sharing policy network between agents to 
ensure that local information can be utilized to obtain the decision in the 
energy management of power and transportation coupling networks. 
However, the parameters of the sharing policy network need to broad -
cast to all local agents through communication equipment. Due to the 
huge number of parameters in neural networks, broadcasting parameter 
information may burden the communication bandwidth, which may 
result in communication delays and data loss. Therefore, this approach 
is not an ideal choice. 
The approaches that follow the centralized training and decentral -
ized execution manner are good choices to avoid privacy leakages and

reduce communication costs. Specifically, the actor-critic architecture 
provides the critic network with rich extra information to stimulate the 
actor network ’ s improvement. This technique allows each agent ’ s actor 
network to maintain a coordinated interaction with others even when it 
is just dependent on local information at the execution stage [17] . By 
utilizing this type of approach, MMG ’ s energy management can be 
accomplished in a totally decentralized manner. This results in a fresh 
guideline for research on MMG energy management, taking into account 
single-point failure avoidance, privacy protection, minimizing commu -
nication costs associated with communication device deployment, and 
real-time responsiveness to optimization demand. Therefore, in recent 
years, there have been many literatures on this topic. In [23] , multi- 
agent asynchronous advantage actor-critic (MAA3C)-based approach is 
used to build an energy scheduling model for the MG-powered multi- 
access edge computing network. A multi-agent trust region policy 
optimization (MATRPO)-enabled MMG system is developed in [24] to 
minimize total costs and improve grid reliability. Ref. [25] proposes a 
PPO with parameter sharing-based MADRL approach for the real-time 
automatic routing and scheduling problem of multiple electric vehi -
cles in the coupled power-transportation network. In [26] , a multi-agent 
proximal policy optimization (MAPPO)-based approach is proposed for 
the objective of MEMG system resilience enhancement. 
The above mentioned actor-critic MADRL approaches belong to on- 
policy. Compared to on-policy MADRL approaches, the data used for 
the training of off-policy MADRL approaches can be from self-generated 
and external, with more abundant means of utilizing historical data. 
Therefore, the latter have higher data utilization rates than the former, 
and their use in optimizing energy management is also more common. A 
multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG)-based energy 
management is proposed in [27] to efficiently coordinate dispatchable 
units to meet the load and reduce operating costs in MG. In [28] , the 
MADDPG-based approach is proposed to manage the energy of multiple 
energy hubs (EHs) with multiple energies. In [29] , a MADDPG-based 
approach is proposed to reduce multiple MGs own energy bills and cut 
down the load on the main utility grid. In [30] , multi-agent twin delayed 
deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3)-based approach is pro -
posed to optimize energy trading of MMG with CHP. Ref. [31] proposes 
a MATD3 with attention mechanism-based approach to manage the 
multiple energies in the MMG system. In order to manage the multiple 
energies involved in the MMG system and reduce energy costs and 
carbon emissions, [32] proposes a MATD3-based approach. As a means 
of controlling MMG ’ s economic frequency, a multi-agent soft actor critic 
(MASAC)-based approach is presented in [33] . In [34] , a MASAC-based 
approach is proposed to manage the energy of MMG with CHP. In [35] , 
the multi-actor-attention-critic (MAAC)-based approach is proposed to 
manage the energy of multiple EHs to achieve the minimization of en -
ergy costs under different demands. A MAAC-based approach is pro -
posed in [36] to manage energy in the EHs. 
To highlight the contributions of this paper, existing literature 
associated with the energy management problems of MG-like has been 
systematically organized in Table 1 . 
Firstly, compared with [18 – 22] , this paper utilizes MADRL with off- 
policy actor-critic framework to manage the energy of MMG system. The 
MADRL with actor-critic framework features centralized training and 
decentralized execution. This allows the actor network of each MG 
controller to obtain a coordinated schedule plan even when only local 
information is available at the time of execution. 
Secondly, despite the advantages indicated, Refs. [23 – 36] have 
certain drawbacks: since the reward function is calculated using the 
power and thermal flows, the premise that one has accurate knowledge 
of the parameters and topology of the electricity and heat networks 
remains. However, it is hard to make accurate physical models of real- 
world systems ’ electrical and thermal systems. For electrical system, it 
is sometimes difficult for operators to be aware of the precision line 
parameters and topology [37,38] . Additionally, it is challenging to 
accurately estimate these characteristics of electrical system because it 
either necessitates a large number of time-stamped measurements or the 
complete measured values of the phasor measurement unit. The former 
may take a lengthy time, whereas the latter is seldom used in reality. For 
thermal systems, accuracy in pipe parameters and topology is also 
required for thermal flow computation, similar to electrical systems. 
Because thermal systems have things like complicated response mech -
anisms, high non-linearity, significant lag, etc., it is hard to get the exact 
parameters of the pipes in the system. In addition, because the con -
sumers are typically widely distributed in the heat network, the topol -
ogy of the secondary pipelines is rather complex [39] . These reasons 
bring challenges for accurately establishing the mathematical model of 
the real-world heat network. Compared with [23 – 36] , the proposed

control framework include the surrogate model to simulate the power 
flow and thermal flow calculation processes. Given the limited historical 
data available to build the surrogate model for the MMG system, unlike 
normal deep learning technologies, the proposed surrogate model with 
few-shot learning characteristic is capable of constructing ideal mapping 
relationships between input data and output power and thermal flow 
results utilizing relatively few data points. This eliminates the need for 
precise model parameters of electricity network and heat network, 
which are notoriously hard to come by and are subject to a wide range of 
practical errors. 
Finally, most studies have focused on altering the architecture of 
critic networks in order to enhance coordination among the agents, 
without delving into the potential of actor networks to improve the 
energy management of MMG [23 – 36] . Unlike individual MG optimiza -
tion, the action space in the multi-agent situation grows exponentially as 
the number of MG rises. A broader action space would make it more 
difficult for agents to uncover excellent control strategy by naive trial 
and error, especially in the coordinated scenario [40] , which readily 
leads to premature convergence to the local optimal solution. These is -
sues may restrict the use of MADRL to energy management of MMG. To 
this end, a novel exploration mechanism is introduced in the proposed 
control framework to avoid convergence prematurely to a local opti -
mum due to the huge action space in energy management of the MMG 
system optimized by a multi-agent control framework. As opposed to 
traditional action space noise (ASN) that is added directly to the action 
[23 – 36] , the proposed exploration mechanism is deployed as follow: the 
gated recurrent network (GRU) is firstly utilized to get a representation 
of historical information for the actor network to overcome the negative 
impact brought by the time series data (TSD) from the input state on the 
decision-making process, then, the parameter space noise (PSN) is 
deployed in the parameters of actor network to increase the scope of 
decision-making space exploration. In the meantime, the deep dense 
architecture in reinforcement learning (D2RL) is deployed in the actor 
network to mitigate the training instability and inefficiency caused by 
noise. 
In this paper, a physics-model-free control framework for the energy 
management of MMGs with heat-electricity energy is developed to 
minimize the operation cost while satisfying the voltage limitation, 
which includes the proposed surrogate model and the MADRL approach. 
The main contributions and salient features of this paper are listed as 
follows:  
1) To simulate the power flow and thermal flow calculation processes, 
two categories of surrogate models are trained using sparse varia -
tional Gaussian processes (SVGP). Using Bayesian theory-based 
technique, only a small amount of historical data is needed to suc -
cessfully detect the mapping connection between input and desired 
output.  
2) A novel exploration mechanism incorporating historical information 
representation is proposed to embed into the actor network. The 
GRU is utilized to get a representation of historical information for 
the actor network to overcome the negative impact brought by the 
TSD from the input state on the decision-making process. For multi- 
agent scenarios, the PSN is utilized to construct effective exploration 
mechanisms in order to avoid premature convergence to a local 
optimum. In addition, the D2RL is deployed in actor network to 
improve the training instability and inefficiency caused by the 
introduction of noise. PSN and D2RL are complementary because 
PSN acts at the parameter level while D2RL establishes a more 
complicated and effective parametric link relationship, thereby 
increasing the exploratory action potential while ensuring training 
stability and efficiency.  
3) The proposed control framework does not necessitate real-time 
optimization of the complex MMG energy management problem, 
as is the case with model-based approaches. The proposed control 
framework enables MG controllers to construct decision-making 
functions offline and then deploy them online, allowing for fully 
decentralized selection of the optimum energy management based 
on the most up-to-date system data. 
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section II introduces 
the mathematical formulations of MMG system and the optimization 
problem. In Section III, the optimization problem is reformulated as 
Markov games and an introduction to the proposed control framework is 
provided. Section IV analyses the numerical simulation results. The 
conclusion of the paper is summarized in Section V. 
2. System modeling descriptions 
2.1. Interconnected MMG with CHP model 
An illustration of a grid interconnected MMG with CHP system is 
shown in Fig. 1 . The number of MG is denoted as g ∈ { 1 , 2 , 3 , ..., G } . The 
g -th MG is made up of a heat and electricity network. The heat network is 
made up of CHP, power to heat (PtH) unit (such as heat pump), and 
thermal load. The electricity network is made up of diesel generator 
(DEG), renewable energy (such as solar and wind energy), energy stor -
age system (ESS), and electrical load. The individual MGs are integrated 
into an interconnected MMG system by the power line (black line) and 
heat pipe (red line), allowing for the exchange of electrical and thermal 
energy between the different MGs. Typically, there are circuit breakers 
as ON or OFF switches in the MMG system. This paper assumes circuit 
breakers are always ON to guarantee energy exchange.

2.3. Heat network modelling 
A heat network typically consists of one source node and multiple 
intermediate/load nodes linked by primary network and secondary 
network. The primary network is known as the generation-side network, 
while the secondary network is known as the consumption-side network. 
During the thermal energy transfer process, water is used to transport 
thermal energy from the supply pipes in the primary network to the 
thermal exchanger in the secondary network, where the thermal energy 
is distributed to all load nodes causing the transmitted water to undergo 
a drastic temperature shift. Finally, the thermal circulation is completed 
when the water travels back through the return pipes [41] .

One phenomenon is that, despite having the same number of updates 
each time, a DRL-based approach ’ s final performance will not be the 
same in these times. In other words, the excellent performance of a DRL- 
based approach may be accidental. Due to the nature of DRL optimiza -
tion, there is sometimes a situation where it is difficult to escape after 
falling into a local optimal trap. In the process of agent falling into the 
trap for a long time, gradient information that may have a persistent 
negative impact on the update of parameters will accumulate. The 
negative impacts brought about by gradient information in parameter 
updates are difficult to erase, even when new gradient information that 
may have a positive impact on parameter updates is introduced. Similar 
deceptive traps are very common in complex problem optimization, 
which is why the reward curve changes from stable convergence to 
difficult convergence when DRL with poor optimization ability is 
applied in environments with increasing optimization difficulty [59] . 
The research of this paper involves internal multi-energy allocations 
within individual MGs, external multilateral multi-energy interactions 
among interconnected MMGs, and energy trading between MMGs and 
the distribution network. In this context, any decision will have multiple 
impacts for the MMG system, which increases the difficulty of the 
agent ’ s seeking optimization in the decision space. Thus, the above 
mentioned phenomenon is more serious in the considered multi-agent 
environments of this paper. In order to verify the performance stabil -
ity of the proposed control framework, box plots of proposed control 
framework and baselines are provided in Fig. 5 . As the figure shows, the 
TD3 has the worst stability due to its lack of coordination. With the 
introduction of a coordinated mechanism, the MATD3 is capable of 
achieving better and more stable performance than the TD3. The 
experiment results show that the multi-agent control problem in the 
coordinated environment needs to introduce the mechanism of coordi -
nated agent interaction into the control algorithm. The advantage of this 
is that it can avoid the negative impact on the parameter update of the 
control algorithm caused by falling into the local optimal trap frequently 
and for a long time. Further, the MASAC approach can have better 
performance than the MATD3 approach due to the introduction of en -
tropy. Through the comparison of the performance of MASAC and 
MAAC, it is known that the use of attention mechanism can enhance the 
coordinated relationships between agents, thus reducing the accumu -
lation of negative gradient information caused by falling into the local 
optimal trap, and further improving the performance and stability of the 
control algorithm. Furthermore, the proposed MADRL approach and 
physics-model-free control framework not only achieve the lowest cost 
but also have the most stable performances among various approaches, 
which demonstrating that (1) The desired results achieved by the pro -
posed MADRL approach are not accidental. The efficiently designed 
exploration mechanism incorporating historical information represen -
tation can ensure the MADRL approach gets rid of the deceptive trap as 
much as possible. Thus, the stability of the desired performance ach -
ieved by the proposed MADRL approach can be guaranteed; (2) In the 
training of DRL agents, the surrogate model can provide a precise 
reward signal for the agents, thus resulting in the proposed control 
framework having similar performance and stability to the proposed 
MADRL approach that relies on physics models. It is evident from this 
that the proposed control framework is effective.
